gate1.note:
GATE 1 APPROVED - round 4. Human decision; the stopping rule was approve-eligible.

RULE: 1 blocking finding, owned by pack-writer; 7 worth a look; 0 blocking
findings owned by `nothing`. Linter 0 errors / 0 warnings. Sessions 37 / 38.5 /
35.5 against the 40 cap, setup session at 2 cuts against 3. 16 criteria, 8 cuts,
all on distinct grading signatures. code_checks: ["utc-dates"] declared.

VERIFIED BY THE ROUND-4 SPEC BREAKER, re-derived rather than trusted: 2026-08-26
is a Wednesday, 2026-08-30 that week's Sunday, 2026-08-31 the Monday of the
2026-09-06 week; seed streaks 5/0/0/1; every toggle expectation arithmetics out.
Critically, it emptied each declared cut of each of the 16 criteria in turn with
the rest filled: all 38 dependencies are load-bearing and no criterion is
satisfied by a proper subset. That is the recipe-box c-3-2 blind spot checked
exhaustively by hand, and it is the strongest evidence any spec here has carried.

ACCEPTED WITH EYES OPEN - three findings owned by `nothing` are being shipped:

  B2 - cut-board-click never mentions the response status, so a student who
       fills it before cut-api-toggle clicks a cell, takes the 501 fallback body
       into `habits` state, and the board dies mid-session. The spec spells this
       out for the other screen and is silent here. WATCH FOR THIS AT GATE 3:
       the pack must not present cut-board-click before cut-api-toggle.
  B3 - habit-name on / is declared in spec.md and spec.json and graded by no
       criterion, while every other board element is pinned. An unlabelled board
       ships 16/16 green. WATCH FOR THIS AT GATE 3: look at the board.
  B4 - "app/.gitignore must contain exactly these two lines" would drop
       *.tsbuildinfo. Made moot in the harness instead: build artifacts are now
       excluded unconditionally.

  A1 (blocking, pack-writer) - the spec claims APP_DIR names the right directory
       in all three runs. The pipeline sets it for its own two only; a student
       running pytest by hand has none. Corrected in CONTRACT.md and the verifier
       skill/agent to Path(os.environ.get("APP_DIR", os.getcwd())), so the
       Verifier will write the fallback even though the spec sentence overstates
       it. The pack must document the student's run.

HARNESS CHANGES THIS SPEC DEPENDS ON, all landed before approval:
  - test_runner passes APP_DIR alongside BASE_URL
  - cutter and deploy_check honour app/.gitignore, so the live store does not

  - build artifacts (*.tsbuildinfo, .DS_Store) excluded unconditionally
  - code_check.py runs named static checks at step 6; utc-dates owns the
    timezone rule that had no checker
  - selftest 183/183

ROUND HISTORY: findings 12 -> 7 -> 6 -> 8, blocking-and-unowned 1 -> 1 -> 1 -> 0.
Three of the findings across rounds 3 and 4 were defects in the pipeline or in my
own briefs, not in the spec.

gate2.note:
GATE 2 APPROVED. 16/16 criteria pass, 0 builder retries, 0 verifier retries.

VERIFIED BEYOND THE COUNT, by hand after the workflow returned:

  - Every one of the 16 criteria has its own named test in coverage.json.
  - The suite is RE-RUNNABLE: 16/16 on three consecutive runs in the same
    working copy. Round 2's A3 finding said this spec would pass once and fail
    on the second run; the reset-every-test rule fixed it. This is what the
    nightly watchdog depends on.
  - code_checks ["utc-dates"] ran live for the first time: 0 violations. And
    lib/week.ts:32 reads `(tracked.getUTCDay() + 6) % 7` - the exact Monday-first
    correction that round 2's A1 said would ship broken without a Sunday
    fixture, with a comment explaining why. c-1-6 and the static check both did
    their job.
  - verify/helpers.py:36 resolves the store as
    Path(os.environ.get("APP_DIR", os.getcwd())) - the fallback idiom, so the
    student's own pytest run works with no environment. The round-4 A1
    correction propagated from CONTRACT.md into the suite.
  - 8 of 8 cut markers present, balanced, none nested, every declared id found
    exactly once. scan_return_safety: 0 violations, every return outside its
    markers.
  - No spec drift: still 6691dad5c499, the hash frozen at Gate 1.
  - app/.gitignore is `data/habits.json` + `!data/habits.seed.json`, and only
    data/habits.seed.json would ship. It does NOT list *.tsbuildinfo, which was
    round 4's B4 - moot because the harness now excludes build artifacts
    unconditionally.

THE TWO ACCEPTED RISKS DID NOT LAND IN THE FINAL CODE:
  - B3: habit-name IS rendered on the board (app/page.tsx:70, with the testid),
    though no criterion grades it. The gap is real; the Builder did not fall in.
  - B2: the click handler DOES guard on response.ok, commented "on anything but
    a 200 the board is left exactly as it was".

CARRIED TO GATE 3 - read these, they are not settled:
  1. B2 IS STILL LIVE FOR THE STUDENT. That response.ok guard sits INSIDE
     cut-board-click, so the student writes it, and the hint never mentions
     status: "POST { date } ... and set the habits state to the same 4 rows with
     only the clicked habit replaced". A student who fills cut-board-click
     before cut-api-toggle and omits the guard takes the 501 fallback body into
     `habits` state and the board dies mid-session. THE PACK MUST NOT PRESENT
     cut-board-click BEFORE cut-api-toggle.
  2. B3: look at the board in the pack's screenshots or description. An
     unlabelled board would have shipped 16/16 green.
  3. A1 (blocking, owned pack-writer): the pack must document the student's own
     pytest run, since APP_DIR is set only by the pipeline's two runs.
  4. B7: session 3 declares node `fs` as a concept but no cut opens writeStore.
     Either the pack teaches it from given code or the concept list is wrong.

gate3.note:
GATE 3 APPROVED, and shipped. Human decision.

STEP 8: 8 cuts, 0 cutter retries. skeleton-check ok, 16 of 16 checked, 0
mismatches, partial_state_risks [] and typecheck_fail_open false - tsc really
ran. The skeleton run is 0 pass / 16 fail with every cut open, which is exactly
what it must be.

STEP 10: deploy clean in 10.7s, all 5 steps ok, no install advisories
(next 15.5.24), live preview served.

STEP 9: pack is 5 files / 1743 lines. The Pack Writer verified its own output:
it extracted every fenced ts/tsx/json block and matched it against app/ and
skeleton/ with 0 unmatched, so no snippet was retyped from memory, and all 8
quoted TODO(...) lines match skeleton/ byte for byte.

FIRST PROJECT WITH A MUTABLE FILE STORE, and the runtime-state handling held:
skeleton/data/ ships habits.seed.json and NOT habits.json.

ACCEPTED WITH EYES OPEN - SESSION 3 IS 47 MINUTES AGAINST THE 40 CAP.
Third consecutive project with an overrun found at step 9. The spec linter
estimated 35.5, so the E111/W112 minute rule - built precisely to prevent this -
was out by 11.5 minutes and did not fire. Cause is identified: the model charges
a flat 6 minutes per cut, and cut-api-toggle is 20 lines with three branches and
an ordering rule between the 400 and 404 checks. Cut size is not knowable at
step 2, because no code exists there.

Approved anyway because the disclosure is materially better than the two
previous projects': session-3.md opens with "the plan below comes to 47 minutes,
7 over the cap", names three trims totalling exactly 7 minutes, states that none
of them touch anything graded, and carries a second fully-written 40-minute
table. The instructor is given a rehearsed alternative, not a warning.

FOR THE SPEC OWNER, if this project is ever revised: session 1 correctly carries
the setup with only 2 cuts; session 3 is where the third cut should have been
dropped, or the toggle route split in two.

TWO BEHAVIOURS NO TEST CATCHES, both written into the guide rather than left to
be discovered:
  1. Filling cut-board-click before cut-api-toggle puts the 501 body
     {"error":"not implemented"} into `habits` state, the next render calls
     .days.map on undefined, and the board disappears. This is Gate 1's B2, and
     the guide now teaches the fill order and the if (response.ok) guard
     together. It was carried here from the Gate 2 note deliberately.
  2. A toggleDate written with push/splice passes every criterion, because the
     caller assigns the result straight back over habit.doneDates so the mutated
     array is the same array. The guide says so and gives the reason to teach the
     pure version anyway.

GATE 1 FINDINGS OWNED BY PACK-WRITER, both resolved from the code:
  A1 - the student's own pytest run needs BASE_URL and must be run from the
       copy's root; APP_DIR exists only for the pipeline's two runs. Documented
       in README.md with the venv/chromium setup, the exact command, and both
       failure modes as separate troubleshooting entries.
  B7 - session 3 declares node fs but the student writes none of it. Kept as a
       named 3-minute read-along, stated plainly, and made trim #1.

HARNESS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS GATE: round 4's B4 was not moot after
all. I had said unconditional build-artifact exclusion covered it; it does not,
because step 8's own tsc typecheck and skeleton build write artifacts INTO
skeleton/ after the copy is made. tip-split's tsconfig.tsbuildinfo is git-tracked
to this day. cutter.sweep_generated now sweeps them once the checks that needed
them have passed; the skeleton was regenerated and shipped clean. selftest
186/186.
